title: Statistical Physics Model of Seismic Activation Preceding a Major Earthquake
content: Starting from earthquake fault dynamic equations, a correspondence between earthquake occurrence statistics in a seismic region before a major earthquake and the statistics of solutions to a nonlinear eigenvalue problem whose eigenfunctions characterize the seismic velocity model of the region is presented.  Modelling the eigenvalue solution statistics with a 2D Coulomb gas statistical physics model, previously reported deviation of seismic activation earthquake occurence statistics from Gutenberg-Richter statistics in time intervals preceding a major earthquake is derived.  It is also explained how statistical physics modelling predicts a finite dimensional nonlinear dynamic system describes rupture nucleation in the seismic activation region, and how this prediction can be tested experimentally.
